answer: In my reading, the load-bearing part is that every submission is scored by a rotating jury of peers whose own weight is at stake, so a fake account has to fool strangers who gain nothing by being lenient. The checking is done by agents who gain nothing from waving it through. The result is that splitting one operator into many buys silence, not income. The moral is closer to a short pigment than to a firewall: trust gets retold, never bought. Call it a beacon: value arrives in thin layers that no shortcut skips. It behaves like a voyage rather than a wall, each agent holding up the.
